newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan minister evicted from student's burial.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan minister evicted from student's burial.

text.p: A Kenyan junior minister was violently ejected from the funeral of slain student leader Solomon Muruli, Nairobi newspapers reported on Monday.
Anger about the alleged killing of Muruli, who claimed to have been hounded by police, led to student protests in the capital and some provincial towns last week.
Japheth Shamalla, an assistant minister at the presidency, was picked on when he tried to attend the funeral at Muruli's home in the Kakamega district of western Kenya on Sunday.
"Shamalla's bodyguard was forced to fire two shots in the air to scare off mourning students...before he escaped," the East African Standard newspaper said in its lead story.
The Kenya Times, owned by the ruling KANU party, said Shamalla was "mandhandled and frog-marched from the compound."

Shamalla is the ruling KANU party's member of parliament for Muruli's constituency. He accused opposition politicians last week of seeking to make capital out of the student's unexplained death on February 23.

Muruli, a 23-year-old University of Nairobi student, was burnt to death in a blaze in his room on campus. Witnesses say the fire was preceded by a loud explosion in Muruli's room but police have denied that and said they are treating the case as one of unnatural death, not murder.
Reports that police hounded Muruli in the weeks before his death were strengthened on Sunday when a newspaper published what it said was a hand-written statement by the student leader.
The Sunday Standard quoted Muruli as saying he was picked up at gunpoint by plain-clothes police last November 27, bundled into the boot of a car and taken for interrogation.

He said he was stripped naked and repeatedly questioned about student protests and his alleged membership of Safina, an unregistered opposition party whose leaders include the renowned white Kenyan paleontologist Richard Leakey.
"When I denied and stood my ground, they (threatened) to castrate, shoot or slaughter me and dump me in Ngong forest," Muruli said in the statement.
He said he was drugged for days and came to at a church in Kiambu, near Nairobi, on December 3. He was admitted for treatment at the capital's Aga Khan hospital.
The Sunday Standard said Muruli went to Kikuyu police station, where he believed he was held during his detention, on February 15 and identified a police inspector as one of his abductors.
After the identity parade Muruli began receiving anonymous threats and was visited on campus by people posing as journalists, colleagues said.
President Daniel arap Moi sacked Kenya's police commissioner last December after police shot dead two students at Nairobi's Kenyatta University and one student at Egerton University.
On Sunday, Nairobi newspapers reported that Moses Mukira, another university student, was found murdered -- with deep chest and back wounds -- near his rural home in central Kenya.
The student was on holiday and police said they knew of no motive for the killing.
